disposition_reason: Measures 18 trace elements in pollen stored by honey bees, bumble bees and red mason bees at 128 European crop sites; the main text prints only a few medians (Al, As, Pb, V, Cu), with the rest in figures and supplementary tables.

study.design: pan-European field monitoring (PoshBee project): sentinel colonies/nests at 128 sites (16 per country, apple orchards and oilseed rape fields along a land-use gradient)
study.origin: Estonia, Sweden, Ireland, United Kingdom, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Spain
study.method: ICP-MS (Agilent 7700x) after microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion; Hg by direct mercury analyzer (DMA-80)
lod: LODs/LOQs in Supplementary Table S1 (not available)
study.qa: ISO/IEC 17025 accredited; EURL-MN proficiency tests; CRMs BCR-185r bovine liver and TORT-3; SRM 1643f for calibration; recoveries in Table S1 (not available)

controls.control: crop type: apple orchard vs oilseed rape field
controls.outcome: Cu median in honey bee stored pollen 8.08 (apple) vs 7.02 µg/g ww (rape); linked by authors to copper fungicide use in orchards; Pb, Cd and As not significantly different by crop type

unresolved: Cd, Hg, Cr, Ni and other element medians for stored pollen are only in Figs. 3-4 and supplementary tables; figure values not read.
Honey bee worker body concentrations (dry weight) are biological samples, not findings.
Sampling year not stated in the main text (PoshBee project).
Stored pollen is hive/nest material for bee exposure assessment, not retail bee pollen.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Bee acute and chronic dietary exposure from stored pollen (µg/bee) and %LD50; e.g., honey bee chronic Cd exposure 0.00058 µg/bee (0.0001% of LDD50)
